correctness.rationale: The quadratic form is strictly positive since the cycle is connected and has a killed vertex. The minimum principle gives entrywise nonnegativity of the inverse, and symmetry identifies both induced endpoint norms with max u for the solution u of the killed Poisson equation with right side 1 (also the mean lifetime). Summing the equation fixes the mean trap value at q/kappa. On each arc of length ell the solution is the linear endpoint interpolation plus j(ell-j)/2. The symmetric two central positions, including both endpoints at ell=1, have average equal to the mean of their endpoint trap values plus floor(ell^2/4)/2. Averaging over all arcs counts each trap twice. Discrete convexity follows from the nondecreasing forward differences ceil(ell/2) of floor(ell^2/4); at mean gap q it gives the sharp geometric lower bound. Rotational symmetry of equal gaps makes all trap values identical, attaining the bound. The one-trap arc closes at the same vertex, and all traps gives 1/kappa. Nothing requires uniqueness of the optimal configuration.

value.rationale: Worst-case mean lifetime is a natural performance criterion for spatially deployed imperfect traps. The theorem computes it exactly for the best configuration across all common finite strengths and separates absorption cost from discrete diffusion cost, with the same optimal deployment throughout. Neither a mean-start statistic nor a spectral decay-rate estimate answers this placement question.
